en: I'm honored to be with you today for your commencement from one of the finest universities in the world.
zh: 今天，我很荣幸能和各位在一起，参加你们从世界上最优秀的大学之一毕业的典礼。

en: Truth be told, I never graduated from college.
zh: 说实话，我从来没有大学毕业过。

en: and this is the closest I've ever gotten to a college graduation.
zh: 而今天，是我离大学毕业典礼最近的一次。

en: Today, I want to tell you three stories from my life.
zh: 今天，我想给你们讲三个我人生中的故事。

en: That's it. No big deal.
zh: 就这些。没什么大道理。

en: Just three stories. The first story is about connecting the dots.
zh: 只是三个故事。第一个故事，是关于把生命中的点滴连接起来。

en: I dropped out of Reed College after the first six months.
zh: 我在里德学院读了六个月后就退学了。

en: but then stayed around as a drop-in for another 18 months or so before I really quit.
zh: 但后来又以旁听生的身份在那里待了大约十八个月，才真正离开。

en: So why'd I drop out?
zh: 那么，我为什么要退学呢？

en: It started before I was born.
zh: 这件事在我出生前就开始了。

en: My biological mother was a young, unwed graduate student.
zh: 我的生母当时是一位年轻的未婚研究生。

en: and she decided to put me up for adoption.
zh: 她决定把我送给别人收养。

en: She felt very strongly that I should be adopted by college graduates,
zh: 她非常坚持，我应该被大学毕业的人收养。

en: so everything was all set for me to be adopted at birth by a lawyer and his wife.
zh: 所以，一切都已经安排好了，我一出生就会被一位律师和他的妻子收养。

en: Except that when I popped out, they decided at the last minute
zh: 可是，当我出生的时候，他们在最后一刻决定，

en: that they really wanted a girl.
zh: 他们其实想要一个女孩。

en: So my parents, who were on a waiting list, got a call in the middle of the night asking,
zh: 于是，我的养父母，当时还在等候名单上，半夜接到了一个电话，问他们：

en: We've got an unexpected baby boy.
zh: 我们这里突然有了一个男婴。

en: Do you want him?
zh: 你们想要他吗？

en: They said, of course.
zh: 他们说，当然要。

en: My biological mother found out later.
zh: 我的生母后来发现，

en: that my mother had never graduated from college and.
zh: 我的养母从未大学毕业，

en: that my father had never graduated from high school.
zh: 我的养父甚至从未高中毕业。

en: She refused to sign the final adoption papers.
zh: 她拒绝在最终的收养文件上签字。

en: She only relented a few months later when my parents promised that I would go to college.
zh: 几个月后，在我的养父母承诺我将来一定会上大学之后，她才让步。

en: This was the start in my life.
zh: 这就是我人生的开端。

en: And 17 years later, I did go to college.
zh: 十七年后，我确实上了大学。

en: But I naively chose a college that was almost as expensive as Stanford.
zh: 但我很天真地选择了一所几乎和斯坦福一样昂贵的大学。

en: And all of my working class parents' savings were being spent on my college tuition.
zh: 我工薪阶层父母一生的积蓄，全都花在了我的大学学费上。

en: After six months, I couldn't see the value in it.
zh: 六个月后，我看不出这件事有什么价值。

en: I had no idea what I wanted to do with my life.
zh: 我完全不知道自己的人生想做什么。

en: and no idea how college was going to help me figure it out.
zh: 也不知道大学要怎样帮我弄明白这一点。

en: And here I was, spending all of the money my parents had saved their entire life.
zh: 而我却正在花掉父母一辈子攒下来的所有钱。

en: So I decided to drop out and trust that it would all work out okay.
zh: 所以我决定退学，并相信一切最终都会好起来。

en: It was pretty scary at the time.
zh: 当时这确实让我很害怕。

en: but looking back, it was one of the best decisions I ever made.
zh: 但现在回头看，那是我做过的最好的决定之一。

en: The minute I dropped out.
zh: 从我退学的那一刻起，

en: I could stop taking the required classes that didn't interest me.
zh: 我就可以不再去上那些我不感兴趣的必修课。

en: and begin dropping in on the ones that looked far more interesting.
zh: 转而去旁听那些看起来有趣得多的课程。

en: It wasn't all romantic.
zh: 当然，这一切并不浪漫。

en: I didn't have a dorm room, so I slept on the floor in friends' rooms.
zh: 我没有宿舍，所以只能睡在朋友房间的地板上。

en: I returned coke bottles for the five-cent deposits to buy food with.
zh: 我靠退还可乐瓶换回五美分押金，用这些钱来买吃的。

en: And I would walk the seven miles across town every Sunday night.
zh: 每个星期天晚上，我都会步行七英里穿过整座城。

en: to get one good meal a week at the Hare Krishna temple.
zh: 去哈瑞奎师那神庙吃上一周里唯一一顿像样的饭。

en: I loved it. And much of what I stumbled into by following my curiosity and intuition turned out to be priceless later on.
zh: 但我热爱这一切。而很多我凭着好奇心和直觉偶然走进的东西，后来都证明是无价的。

en: Let me give you one example.
zh: 我给你们举一个例子。

en: Reed College at that time offered perhaps the best calligraphy instruction in the country.
zh: 当时，里德学院提供的书法课程，可能是全美国最好的。

en: Throughout the campus, every poster, every label on every drawer was beautifully hand-calligraphed.
zh: 校园里的每一张海报、每一个抽屉上的标签，都有漂亮的手写书法。

en: Because I had dropped out and didn't have to take the normal classes,
zh: 因为我已经退学，不必再上那些常规课程，

en: I decided to take a calligraphy class to learn how to do this.
zh: 我决定去上一门书法课，学习它是怎么做到的。

en: I learned about serif and sans serif typefaces.
zh: 我学到了衬线字体和无衬线字体。

en: about varying the amount of space between different letter combinations, about what makes great typography great.
zh: 学到了如何调整不同字母组合之间的间距，也学到了是什么让优秀的字体排印真正优秀。

en: It was beautiful, historical, artistically subtle in a way that science can't capture,
zh: 它美丽、古老，带着一种科学无法捕捉的艺术细腻感。

en: and I found it fascinating.
zh: 而我觉得它迷人极了。

en: None of this had even a hope of any practical application in my life.
zh: 这一切当时看起来，完全不可能在我的人生中有什么实际用途。

en: But ten years later, when we were designing the first Macintosh computer,
zh: 但十年后，当我们设计第一台麦金塔电脑时，

en: it all came back to me.
zh: 这些东西全都回到了我的脑海里。

en: And we designed it all into the Mac.
zh: 于是，我们把它们全部设计进了 Mac 里。

en: It was the first computer with beautiful typography.
zh: 它成了第一台拥有漂亮字体排印的电脑。

en: If I had never dropped in on that single course in college,
zh: 如果我当年没有旁听那门大学课程，

en: the Mac would have never had multiple typefaces or proportionally spaced fonts.
zh: Mac 就不会拥有多种字体，也不会有按比例间距设计的字形。

en: And since Windows just copied the Mac, it's likely that no personal computer would have them.
zh: 而既然 Windows 只是借鉴了 Mac，那么很可能所有个人电脑都不会拥有这些东西。

en: If I had never dropped out, I would have never dropped in on that calligraphy class,
zh: 如果我从未退学，我就不会去旁听那门书法课。

en: and personal computers might not have the wonderful typography that they do.
zh: 个人电脑也可能不会拥有今天这样美妙的字体排印。

en: Of course, it was impossible to connect the dots looking forward when I was in college,
zh: 当然，当我还在大学的时候，不可能向前看就把这些点连接起来。

en: but it was very, very clear looking backwards ten years later.
zh: 但十年后回头看，一切都变得非常非常清楚。

en: Again, you can't connect the dots looking forward.
zh: 再说一次，你无法向前看，把这些点连接起来。

en: You can only connect them looking backwards.
zh: 你只能在回头看时，才把它们连接起来。

en: So you have to trust that the dots will somehow connect in your future.
zh: 所以你必须相信，这些点会在未来以某种方式连接起来。

en: You have to trust in something, your gut, destiny, life, karma, whatever.
zh: 你必须相信某种东西，你的直觉、命运、人生、因果，随便什么。

en: Because believing that the dots will connect down the road.
zh: 因为相信这些点会在未来某一天连接起来，

en: will give you the confidence to follow your heart, even when it leads you off the well-worn path,
zh: 会给你信心去追随自己的内心，即使它带你偏离那条人们走惯的道路。

en: and that will make all the difference.
zh: 而这会让一切变得不同。

en: My second story is about love and loss.
zh: 我的第二个故事，是关于热爱与失去。

en: I was lucky. I found what I loved to do early in life.
zh: 我很幸运。我很早就找到了自己热爱的事情。

en: Woz and I started Apple in my parents' garage when I was 20.
zh: 我二十岁时，沃兹和我在父母家的车库里创办了苹果。

en: We worked hard, and in ten years, Apple had grown from just the two of us in a garage.
zh: 我们努力工作，十年里，苹果从车库里的我们两个人，

en: into a $2 billion company with over 4,000 employees.
zh: 成长为一家市值二十亿美元、拥有四千多名员工的公司。

en: We'd just released our finest creation, the Macintosh, a year earlier.
zh: 就在一年前，我们刚刚发布了我们最优秀的作品——麦金塔电脑。

en: and I'd just turned 30.
zh: 而我也刚刚三十岁。

en: And then I got fired.
zh: 然后，我被解雇了。

en: How can you get fired from a company you started?
zh: 一个人怎么会被自己创办的公司解雇呢？

en: Well, as Apple grew, we hired someone who I thought was very talented to run the company with me.
zh: 事情是这样的，随着苹果的发展，我们请来了一位我认为非常有才华的人，与我一起经营公司。

en: And for the first year or so, things went well.
zh: 最初一年左右，一切都很顺利。

en: But then our visions of the future began to diverge, and eventually we had a falling-out.
zh: 但后来，我们对未来的愿景开始产生分歧，最终闹翻了。

en: When we did, our board of directors sided with him.
zh: 当事情发展到那一步时，董事会站在了他那边。

en: And so at 30, I was out, and very publicly out.
zh: 于是，在三十岁的时候，我出局了，而且是非常公开地出局。

en: What had been the focus of my entire adult life was gone,
zh: 曾经占据我整个成年人生核心位置的东西，消失了。

en: and it was devastating.
zh: 这对我来说是毁灭性的打击。

en: I really didn't know what to do for a few months.
zh: 有好几个月，我真的不知道该怎么办。

en: I felt that I had let the previous generation of entrepreneurs down,
zh: 我觉得自己辜负了上一代创业者。

en: that I had dropped the baton as it was being passed to me.
zh: 仿佛接力棒传到我手中时，我却把它掉在了地上。

en: I met with David Packard and Bob Noyce.
zh: 我去见了戴维·帕卡德和鲍勃·诺伊斯。

en: and tried to apologize for screwing up so badly.
zh: 试着为自己把事情搞得如此糟糕而道歉。

en: I was a very public failure, and I even thought about running away from the Valley.
zh: 我成了一个众所周知的失败者，甚至想过逃离硅谷。

en: But something slowly began to dawn on me.
zh: 但有件事慢慢开始在我心里显现出来。

en: I still loved what I did.
zh: 我仍然热爱自己所做的事情。

en: The turn of events at Apple had not changed that one bit.
zh: 苹果发生的变故，一点也没有改变这一点。

en: I'd been rejected, but I was still in love.
zh: 我被拒绝了，但我仍然深爱着它。

en: And so I decided to start over.
zh: 所以，我决定重新开始。

en: I didn't see it then.
zh: 当时我还看不出来。

en: but it turned out that getting fired from Apple was the best thing that could have ever happened to me.
zh: 但后来证明，被苹果解雇，是发生在我身上最好的事情。

en: The heaviness of being successful was replaced by the lightness of being a beginner again,
zh: 成功所带来的沉重感，被重新成为初学者的轻盈感取代了。

en: less sure about everything.
zh: 我对一切都不再那么确定。

en: It freed me to enter one of the most creative periods of my life.
zh: 这让我获得了自由，进入了人生中最富创造力的时期之一。

en: During the next five years, I started a company named NeXT, another company named Pixar,
zh: 在接下来的五年里，我创办了一家名叫 NeXT 的公司，又创办了另一家名叫皮克斯的公司。

en: and fell in love with an amazing woman who would become my wife.
zh: 还爱上了一位了不起的女人，她后来成了我的妻子。

en: Pixar went on to create the world's first computer-animated feature film, Toy Story,
zh: 皮克斯后来制作了世界上第一部电脑动画长片《玩具总动员》。

en: and is now the most successful animation studio in the world.
zh: 如今，它已经成为世界上最成功的动画工作室。

en: In a remarkable turn of events, Apple bought NeXT, and I returned to Apple.
zh: 在一次非凡的转折中，苹果收购了 NeXT，而我回到了苹果。

en: And the technology we developed at NeXT is at the heart of Apple's current renaissance.
zh: 我们在 NeXT 开发的技术，正是苹果如今复兴的核心。

en: And Lorene and I have a wonderful family together.
zh: 我和劳伦也一起拥有了一个美好的家庭。

en: I'm pretty sure none of this would have happened if I hadn't been fired from Apple.
zh: 我很确定，如果我当年没有被苹果解雇，这一切都不会发生。

en: It was awful tasting medicine, but I guess the patient needed it.
zh: 那是一剂味道糟糕的药，但我想，病人确实需要它。

en: Sometimes life's going to hit you in the head with a brick.
zh: 有时候，人生会拿砖头狠狠砸你的头。

en: Don't lose faith. I'm convinced that the only thing that kept me going was
zh: 不要失去信念。我相信，让我坚持下去的唯一原因，

en: that I loved what I did.
zh: 就是我热爱自己所做的事情。

en: You've got to find what you love, and that is as true for work as it is for your lovers.
zh: 你必须找到你热爱的东西。对工作如此，对你的爱人也是如此。

en: Your work is going to fill a large part of your life,
zh: 你的工作将占据你人生中很大一部分。

en: and the only way to be truly satisfied is to do what you believe is great work.
zh: 而真正获得满足的唯一方式，就是去做你认为伟大的工作。

en: And the only way to do great work is to love what you do.
zh: 而做出伟大工作的唯一方式，就是热爱你所做的事情。

en: If you haven't found it yet, keep looking, and don't settle.
zh: 如果你还没有找到，那就继续寻找，不要将就。

en: As with all matters of the heart, you'll know when you find it.
zh: 就像所有关乎内心的事情一样，当你找到时，你自然会知道。

en: And like any great relationship, it just gets better and better as the years roll on.
zh: 而且像任何美好的关系一样，随着岁月流逝，它只会变得越来越好。

en: So keep looking. Don't settle.
zh: 所以，继续寻找。不要将就。

en: My third story is about death.
zh: 我的第三个故事，是关于死亡。

en: When I was 17, I read a quote that went something like,
zh: 十七岁时，我读到过一句话，大意是：

en: If you live each day as if it was your last.
zh: 如果你把每一天都当作生命中的最后一天来过，

en: someday you'll most certainly be right.
zh: 那么总有一天，你一定会是对的。

en: It made an impression on me.
zh: 这句话给我留下了很深的印象。

en: and since then, for the past 33 years, I've looked in the mirror every morning and asked myself
zh: 从那以后，过去三十三年里，我每天早晨都会看着镜子问自己：

en: if today were the last day of my life, would I want to do what I am about to do today?
zh: 如果今天是我生命中的最后一天，我还会想去做今天将要做的事情吗？

en: And whenever the answer has been no for too many days in a row,
zh: 每当答案连续很多天都是不的时候，

en: I know I need to change something.
zh: 我就知道，我需要做出一些改变。

en: Remembering that I'll be dead soon.
zh: 记住自己很快就会死去，

en: is the most important tool I've ever encountered to help me make the big choices in life.
zh: 是我遇到过的、帮助我做出人生重大选择的最重要工具。

en: Because almost everything, all external expectations, all pride, all fear of embarrassment or failure,
zh: 因为几乎所有东西，所有外界的期待，所有骄傲，所有对尴尬或失败的恐惧，

en: these things just fall away in the face of death.
zh: 在死亡面前都会消散。

en: leaving only what is truly important.
zh: 只留下真正重要的东西。

en: Remembering that you are going to die is the best way I know to avoid the trap of thinking you have something to lose.
zh: 记住自己终将死去，是我知道的避免陷入自己还有什么可失去这种陷阱的最好方法。

en: You are already naked.
zh: 你本来就已经一无所有。

en: There is no reason not to follow your heart.
zh: 所以没有理由不去追随自己的内心。

en: About a year ago, I was diagnosed with cancer.
zh: 大约一年前，我被诊断出患有癌症。

en: I had a scan at 7.30 in the morning, and it clearly showed a tumor on my pancreas.
zh: 我早上七点半做了一次扫描，结果清楚地显示我的胰腺上有一个肿瘤。

en: I didn't even know what a pancreas was.
zh: 我当时甚至不知道胰腺是什么。

en: The doctors told me this was almost certainly a type of cancer that is incurable and
zh: 医生告诉我，这几乎可以确定是一种无法治愈的癌症，

en: that I should expect to live no longer than three to six months.
zh: 我预期最多只能再活三到六个月。

en: My doctor advised me to go home and get my affairs in order,
zh: 我的医生建议我回家，把身后事安排好。

en: which is doctor's code for prepare to die.
zh: 这是医生的委婉说法，意思就是准备去死。

en: It means to try and tell your kids everything.
zh: 这意味着你要试着把所有事情都告诉你的孩子。

en: you thought you'd have the next ten years to tell them in just a few months.
zh: 那些你原以为还有十年时间可以告诉他们的话，现在要在几个月里说完。

en: It means to make sure everything is buttoned up.
zh: 这意味着你要确保一切都安排妥当。

en: so that it will be as easy as possible for your family.
zh: 这样你的家人以后才能尽可能轻松一些。

en: It means to say your goodbyes.
zh: 这意味着你要和人告别。

en: I live with that diagnosis all day.
zh: 我整整一天都带着那个诊断结果生活着。

en: Later that evening, I had a biopsy where they stuck an endoscope down my throat,
zh: 那天晚上晚些时候，我做了一次活检，医生把内窥镜从我的喉咙伸进去，

en: threw my stomach into my intestines.
zh: 穿过我的胃，进入我的肠道。

en: put a needle into my pancreas and got a few cells from the tumor.
zh: 再把一根针插进我的胰腺，从肿瘤里取出一些细胞。

en: I was sedated, but my wife, who was there, told me that
zh: 我当时被麻醉了，但在场的妻子后来告诉我，

en: when they viewed the cells under a microscope, the doctors started crying
zh: 当医生们在显微镜下观察那些细胞时，他们开始哭了。

en: because it turned out to be a very rare form of pancreatic cancer that is curable with surgery.
zh: 因为结果显示，那是一种非常罕见、可以通过手术治愈的胰腺癌。

en: I had the surgery, and thankfully, I'm fine now.
zh: 我做了手术，谢天谢地，现在我很好。

en: This was the closest I've been to facing death.
zh: 这是我离面对死亡最近的一次。

en: and I hope it's the closest I get for a few more decades.
zh: 我希望在接下来的几十年里，这仍然是我离死亡最近的一次。

en: Having lived through it.
zh: 经历过这件事之后，

en: I can now say this to you with a bit more certainty than
zh: 我现在可以更确定地对你们说这些话。

en: when death was a useful but purely intellectual concept.
zh: 比起死亡还只是一个有用但纯粹理性的概念时，要确定得多。

en: No one wants to die.
zh: 没有人想死。

en: Even people who want to go to heaven don't want to die to get there.
zh: 即使是想上天堂的人，也不想通过死亡去那里。

en: And yet, death is the destination we all share.
zh: 然而，死亡是我们所有人共同的终点。

en: No one has ever escaped it.
zh: 从来没有人能逃过它。

en: And that is as it should be.
zh: 这本来也应该如此。

en: because death is very likely the single best invention of life.
zh: 因为死亡很可能是生命中唯一最好的发明。

en: It's life's change agent.
zh: 它是生命的变革推动者。

en: It clears out the old to make way for the new.
zh: 它清除旧事物，为新事物让路。

en: Right now, the new is you.
zh: 现在，新的就是你们。

en: But someday, not too long from now.
zh: 但总有一天，在不久的将来，

en: you will gradually become the old and be cleared away.
zh: 你们也会逐渐变成旧的，然后被清除。

en: Sorry to be so dramatic, but it's quite true.
zh: 抱歉说得这么戏剧化，但这确实是真的。

en: Your time is limited, so don't waste it living someone else's life.
zh: 你们的时间有限，所以不要浪费时间去过别人的人生。

en: Don't be trapped by dogma, which is living with the results of other people's thinking.
zh: 不要被教条束缚，那等于活在别人思考的结果里。

en: Don't let the noise of others' opinions drown out your own inner voice.
zh: 不要让别人观点的噪音，淹没你自己内心的声音。

en: And most important, have the courage to follow your heart and intuition.
zh: 最重要的是，要有勇气追随自己的内心和直觉。

en: They somehow already know what you truly want to become.
zh: 它们不知为何，早已知道你真正想成为什么样的人。

en: Everything else is secondary.
zh: 其他一切都是次要的。

en: When I was young, there was an amazing publication called The Whole Earth Catalog,
zh: 我年轻的时候，有一本很了不起的出版物，叫《全球概览》。

en: which was one of the Bibles of my generation.
zh: 它是我们那一代人的圣经之一。

en: It was created by a fellow named Stuart Brand, not far from here in Menlo Park.
zh: 它由一个名叫斯图尔特·布兰德的人创办，就在离这里不远的门洛帕克。

en: And he brought it to life with his poetic touch.
zh: 他用自己富有诗意的方式，让它鲜活了起来。

en: This was in the late 60s, before personal computers and desktop publishing.
zh: 那是在六十年代末，个人电脑和桌面出版还没有出现之前。

en: So it was all made with typewriters, scissors, and Polaroid cameras.
zh: 所以它完全是用打字机、剪刀和宝丽来相机制作出来的。

en: It was sort of like Google in paperback form 35 years before Google came along.
zh: 它有点像纸质版的 Google，只不过比 Google 早出现了三十五年。

en: It was idealistic, overflowing with neat tools and great notions.
zh: 它充满理想主义，里面有大量有趣的工具和很棒的想法。

en: Stuart and his team put out several issues of The Whole Earth Catalog.
zh: 斯图尔特和他的团队出版了好几期《全球概览》。

en: And then, when it had run its course, they put out a final issue.
zh: 后来，当它完成了自己的使命时，他们推出了最后一期。

en: It was the mid -1970s, and I was your age.
zh: 那是在二十世纪七十年代中期，而我当时和你们现在差不多大。

en: On the back cover of their final issue was a photograph of an early morning country road,
zh: 在最后一期的封底上，有一张清晨乡间道路的照片。

en: the kind you might find yourself hitchhiking on if you were so adventurous.
zh: 如果你足够有冒险精神，那可能就是你会在上面搭车旅行的那种路。

en: Beneath it were the words, stay hungry, stay foolish.
zh: 照片下面写着几个字：求知若饥，虚心若愚。

en: It was their farewell message as they signed off.
zh: 那是他们停刊告别时留下的信息。

en: Stay hungry, stay foolish.
zh: 求知若饥，虚心若愚。

en: And I have always wished that for myself.
zh: 我一直希望自己能做到这一点。

en: And now, as you graduate to begin anew, I wish that for you.
zh: 而现在，当你们毕业并开始新的人生时，我也把这句话送给你们。

en: Stay hungry, stay foolish.
zh: 求知若饥，虚心若愚。

en: Thank you all very much.
zh: 非常感谢大家。
